[[File:RickTocchet2024Feb16.jpg|right|thumb|175px|[[Rick Tocchet]] is the current head coach of the Flyers.]]
The [[Philadelphia Flyers]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Philadelphia]]. They are members of the [[Metropolitan Division]] of the [[National Hockey League]]'s (NHL) [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/info/teams/ |title=Teams – NHL.com |website=National Hockey League |access-date=January 11, 2017}}</ref> The Flyers were founded in 1967 as one of six [[1967 NHL Expansion|expansion teams]], increasing the size of the NHL at that time to 12 teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/winter-classic-facts-to-astound-and-amaze/c-511067 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113133406/https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/winter-classic-facts-to-astound-and-amaze/c-511067 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 13, 2017 |title=Winter Classic Facts to Astound and Amaze |website=Philadelphia Flyers |date=December 25, 2009 |access-date=January 11, 2017}}</ref>

Since the [[Professional sports league organization|franchise]] was established, the team has had 25 [[Coach (ice hockey)|head coaches]],<ref name="Tocchet" /> including [[Fred Shero]], who coached the Flyers to two [[Stanley Cup]]s in 1974 and 1975, and was the inaugural winner of the [[Jack Adams Award]] in [[1973–74 NHL season|1973–74]].<ref name="Adams">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/trophies/adams.html|title=Jack Adams Award|publisher=[[NHL]]|access-date=2011-01-14|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706102444/http://www.nhl.com/trophies/adams.html|archive-date=2008-07-06}}</ref> Three other Flyers coaches have won the Adams Award – [[Pat Quinn (ice hockey)|Pat Quinn]] in [[1979–80 NHL season|1979–80]], [[Mike Keenan]] in [[1984–85 NHL season|1984–85]], and [[Bill Barber]] in [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]].<ref name="Adams" /> The Flyers current head coach is [[Rick Tocchet]].<ref name="Tocchet" />
